supersedes.reason: Sixth Flap interaction risk report (2026-09-03 15:46, rating Low). Three fixes: (1) trigger() picked an action from pre-fee pendingRevenue while _schedule deducted the fee afterward, so a deploy chosen in the band [MIN_DEPLOY, MIN_DEPLOY+fee) spent a real fee and then reverted -- _pickAction now reserves the fee before the threshold check, the same saturating way _schedule subtracts it. (2) the lever-up branch of _rebalance folded the flash build's own 0.3% over-borrow buffer leftover into pendingRevenue without the costBasis decrement the deleverage branch already had, letting a later _deploy inflate costBasis for capital that never raised nav -- now both branches move costBasis and pendingRevenue together, so basis is invariant across any rebalance regardless of direction. (3) found while fixing (2): the lever-up branch could pay a small incidental bounty from that same buffer, contradicting the vault's own 'levering up pays no bounty' documentation -- it now always pays zero there, and the deleverage bounty's basis (the deleveraged notional, not whatever a shrink happens to free) is stated precisely in both the on-chain schema and the README.

retiredNote: Every address this project has ever deployed and replaced. Registering any of them with Flap would bind a token to superseded code. tools/check-docs.py reads this list, so a redeploy updates one file rather than a constant in the checker.

upgradeAuthority.LeverBeacon: owns the vault implementation; Flap Guardian
upgradeAuthority.LeverFactoryBeacon: owns the factory implementation; Flap Guardian
upgradeAuthority.note: Both beacons transfer ownership to the Guardian inside their own constructors, so the deployer never holds upgrade authority for a single block. Nothing else in this project has an owner, admin, or role of any kind.
